_doc: query_alias: a grammar that has no graph/data/queries/<grammar>/ of its own uses the queries of the named one (tsx = typescript plus jsx nodes the queries do not mention). ext/filenames/shebang/rules -> lang. role: code | config | data. family = the key the engine router groups languages by, grammar = tree-sitter grammar name, extractor = module graph.extract.<name> (null = read by the root extractors only). holder_edge = link.py gives every member an edge to the type that holds it (a live member keeps its class alive; the flag works per family). members_by_receiver = the members of a type are named through a receiver only (python, go): link.py skips the class scopes of a bare name seen from a def nested in them, so the type `renderPage` and the method `server.renderPage` stay two nodes (per family). build_twins = the defs of one name in two files of one directory are one symbol, each keeps the other alive (go: files that exclude each other by a GOOS suffix or `//go:build`; per family). copy_twins = a file that sits under another root with the same relative path and the same facts as another file (an overlay, a deploy payload, a vendored copy) is the same module: their defs keep each other alive (N, per family). type_scope = link.py resolves a bare name written in a member to the members of the enclosing type, of its other declarations (partial parts, the class in a header) and of its ancestors, and ties a member declared in its class to its definition written out of class (per family). namespaceless = namespaces are no defs: link.py reads the head of a dotted name no scope knows (`util::helper`, `Ns.Util`) as a namespace and resolves the last part (per family). root_inherit = root kinds that a class derived from the rooted class inherits (a host builds the subclasses of a host base too; per family). native = the extractor parses the file itself, no grammar is needed (yaml: graph.extract.yamlite). in_dir = the language of a file that has none (or is plain data) and sits below a directory of that name. ext rules: a string maps the extension, a list of {re, lang} (content regex on the first 4 KB, first hit wins) ends with the default. crate (a language whose packages are crates, the linker reads it: rust): src = the directory of a package that holds the crate root files, roots = their stems in order of preference (src/lib.rs before src/main.rs; only a package with a library, the first root, can be imported by its name), the package is the directory above src and its name the directory name (`-` -> `_`; the Cargo.toml of a package is not read by the linker: in a repo with a library crate any other head of a use that is not in sysroot is matched by the imported names, N), sysroot = crates of the toolchain that are never a package of the project. file_init: the top-level code of a file (property initializers, script statements) runs when any top-level declaration of the file is used, so the linker adds an implicit edge from each top-level def to its file (and from the file to each top-level property: the initializers run with it). link_group: languages of one group see each other's declarations (Java and Kotlin call each other); default = family. package_dir: a package is its directory (the declaration of a file is found by the directory of its package); package_loose: the declared package need not match the directory (Kotlin), so a named import that no directory explains is bound by the name of the declaration, and a class that a registration file names is found by its simple name when no directory matches. implicit_receiver: a bare name that no scope, import or top-level def answers may be a member of an implicit receiver (an extension function `fun Foo.baz() { bar() }`, a lambda with receiver: apply, with, a DSL builder), so link.py also matches the members of that name (N; per language: another language of the same link group, Scala beside Kotlin, keeps its own scoping). file_facade: suffix of the class that other JVM languages see for the top-level declarations of a file (Util.kt -> UtilKt). link_group "cfg" (yaml, helm-*, make, just, dockerfile, shell): the languages whose names carry a tag (`recipe:test`, `stage:builder`, `job:build`) see each other: a CI line or a shell script that runs `make test` reaches the recipe (names of other languages carry no tag, so the shared table holds no other clash). ambiguous_names: the same as ambiguous for a whole file name (`nginx.conf`: a template with `{{` is plain data, or a Helm template below templates/, anything else is nginx). ambiguous .conf: a template ({{) is plain data, nginx directives make it nginx, anything else is ini. script_ext: extensions of the language that are run as scripts (Gradle build.gradle.kts): such a file is an entry point. entry_re: regexes of the repo-relative path of files that a tool, a server or a framework runs or serves by convention (Rakefile, config.ru, index.php, a Jenkinsfile, flake.nix, BUILD, a served .html page, a SvelteKit +page.svelte): each is an entry point like a script_ext file.

helm-values._doc: Helm values: the cfgkeys of a plain mapping are read by templates only; other yaml has no such reader and gets no keys. readers_dir: the templates must sit beside the file (link.py _extern), otherwise the chart is deployed from elsewhere and the keys are not provably dead

helm-template._doc: a file under a templates/ directory that no language claims (NOTES.txt) or that is plain data (*.conf, *.json, *.toml, *.md ...): Helm renders every file of the directory, so its {{ .Values }} reads count. in_dir: any path segment with that name; YAML and code files keep their language

haproxy._doc: a service config: a soft root; paths of scripts, certificates and error pages as refs (graph.extract.cfgconf)

keepalived._doc: vrrp_script / vrrp_instance defs, track_script refs, notify scripts (graph.extract.cfgconf)

logql._doc: a LogQL query file read by logcli or Grafana: a soft root

jsonnet._doc: a program that jsonnet / tanka renders: a soft root

libsonnet._doc: a library: alive while a jsonnet file imports it

json._doc: json .. cmake: known languages without a graph (role data: nothing reads them, no dc.unsupported-language)
